reconcile.note: Matthew Henry reads the Genesis 6:6 grief as a change in God's dealings with corrupted humanity rather than any reversal of his unchanging mind or his original verdict.

discrepancy.note: Ingersoll argues God's later regret over making humanity was no surprise to an all-knowing deity, undercutting the sincerity of his prior 'very good' verdict.

quotes.text: Of course God knew when he made man, that he would afterwards regret it.
quotes.attr: Robert G. Ingersoll (d. 1899), Some Mistakes of Moses (1879), ch. XVIII, on Genesis 6:6.

sides.snippet: God saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very good.
sides.verseText: God saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. There was evening and there was morning, the sixth day.

sides.snippet: Yahweh was sorry that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him in his heart.
sides.verseText: Yahweh was sorry that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him in his heart.
